method: Separately reviewed original whole-measure guitar accompaniment plan. Grips below are written from standard guitar tuning and triad intervals, not exported from MusicXML. Melody references are independent and live in source-review.json. A chord sounds once per measure, including a shortened pickup; nonchord melody tones act as passing tones or suspensions. These are beginner accompaniments, not historical piano harmonizations.

reviewNotes: All grips contain exactly the major or minor root/third/fifth pitch classes, use one tone per string and keep fretting within frets 0–3.
F is a four-string small barre, not a six-string F barre. The low two strings are omitted. D/Dm omit low E and A; C/Am/A omit low E.

Ash Grove bar 18 is tonic G to support its D–B–G melodic triad. Drink to Me bar 11 uses C to support the E and C melody, resolving to D. Blue Bells uses the early Willig version, with tonic support under its E–E–F–D figure.
Minor-key pieces use E major where G-sharp leads toward A minor. No chord symbol is substituted for actual note events.

Historical phrases are complete within each stated scope. Accompaniment follows every pickup, rest-containing measure and final measure for exactly the melody arrangement timeline. Melody rests do not force the accompaniment to rest.
